To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
partial gastrectomy for benign ulcer disease increases the risk of stomach cancer by 2.5-5 times, the risk depending on the method used.

the risk of developing stomach cancer after partial gastrectomies according to Billroths I and II, respectively, is about 2.5 times higher than in the general population and that the risk increases with the age at operation and the length of the follow-up.
the risk of developing gastric cancer after Billroth I is increased 2-fold and after Billroth II 3-fold, compared to the risk of the general population of the corresponding ages.

the study of the risk of developing gastric cancer after operation for ulcer disease and the possible mechanisms involved in this risk.
the risk of cancer of different sites in the stomach after operation and with the influence of the surgical method, age at operation and follow-up time, and sex of the patient on this risk.
the development of cancer of the gastrointestinal tract, and the results have implications for the choice of treatment and follow-up of patients with ulcer disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the risk of developing gastric cancer after operation for ulcer disease is increased in the long run, but that the increase is not very large and that it is influenced by several factors, both before and after operation.

the risk of developing gastric cancer after partial gastrectomies for ulcer disease is increased, especially for those patients who are operated at a young age for a diagnosis of ulcer disease, and the risk is greatest after Billroth II resections and in the case of male patients.
partial gastrectomy increases the risk of cancer of stomach in patients with peptic ulcer disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the risk of cancer of stomach is significantly increased after partial gastrectomies for ulcer disease, but only after 10-15 years of follow-up.
partial gastrectomy for ulcer disease increases the risk of cancer of stomach in the long-term follow-up.
a partial gastrectomy increases the risk for cancer of the stomach, but the risk varies according to the surgical method and other variables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of surgical procedure is of minor importance compared to the diagnosis of ulcer disease.

the risk of developing gastric cancer is increased in patients who have had a gastrectomy, but the risk is reduced in patients who have been operated on for gastric ulcer and who are followed for a long time.
